summary: Discovery focused on Minnow's need to balance rapid PLG test drives with security requirements. Team prefers time-to-first-token under an hour for devs, evaluating hosted quickstart with free credits first, then a potential reserved/dedicated pilot or VPC/private deploy for PII workloads. transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-10-20 15:00 PDT
Duration: ~48 minutes
Attendees: Alex Chen (Redwood AE), Priya Suresh (Redwood SE), Noah Patel (Redwood CSM), Jacob Rivera (Minnow CTO), Mia Torres (Minnow Eng Manager), Sarah Li (Minnow Head of Data), Ethan Park (Minnow Security)

Auto-summary (auto): Quick discovery. Customer wants fast dev velocity but strong controls. Agrees to trial credits and security papers.

[00:00] Alex Chen: hey everyone thanks for hopping on, um we'll do a quick intro from our side, then Priya will walk through the hosting options and we'll leave time for security and pilot details. uh can you do quick intros?
[00:12] Jacob Rivera: yep jacob here, i'm CTO at Minnow digital, we run real-time summarization for customer emails, lots of PII, so security matters.
[00:20] Mia Torres: Mia, eng manager, i'm running the integration work, would like to see how fast my team can get to first token.
[00:27] Sarah Li: Sarah, head of data, we'll be sending sample anonymized corpora for evals.
[00:33] Ethan Park: Ethan, security, i will own compliance questions.
[00:37] Alex Chen: great thanks, from Redwood we have Priya on infra and Noah for customer success, i'll be your primary AE.
[00:44] Priya Suresh: hi all. quick agenda: 1) hosted quickstart and free credits + ttft (time to first token) 2) tradeoffs between hosted, dedicated, and private (VPC) 3) security checklist 4) pilot next steps. sound good?
[00:55] Jacob Rivera: yep perfect. main constraints: devs need to spin something in a day, we need guardrails for PII, and we care about both latency and cost.

---

[01:20] Priya Suresh: ok hosted quickstart: we give free credits to test the Redwood API — typical flow is sign up, exchange API key, run example curl or SDK snippet. most teams hit first token in 10-40 minutes depending on onboarding. we also have quickstart templates for Node/Python and a postman collection.
[01:45] Mia Torres: 10-40 minutes is great. is there any friction for getting data into the test? like can we mount S3 or do we just POST text?
[01:53] Priya Suresh: usually POST text to our endpoints. for larger datasets we support signed S3 uploads to our sandbox or you can stream. but for dev evals, POST is simplest.
[02:06] Sarah Li: do you allow ephemeral API keys so we can rotate per-dev?
[02:10] Alex Chen: yes we support API key rotation, and you can scope keys to projects. for enterprise we add token-level RBAC but dev teams can use ephemeral keys for quick trials.

[02:25] Jacob Rivera: about hosted environment: what about data retention and logs? we can't keep raw PII in logs longer than 30 days.
[02:33] Priya Suresh: default retention is 30 days for hosted trial logs, customers can request shorter retention; for production we have options to disable logging and enable no-retention modes — we also support bring-your-own-KMS for encryption at rest in private deployments.

[02:50] Ethan Park: and audit logs for requests? we need immutable audit trails.
[02:54] Priya Suresh: yes, audit logs are available in Redwood Console; for hosted we provide a standard audit feed, for Dedicated and Private you can enable an external SIEM sink (syslog/CloudWatch/Stackdriver). we'll share the docs.

---

[03:25] Alex Chen: switching to hosting tradeoffs. Priya, can you outline differences quickly?
[03:28] Priya Suresh: sure. Hosted = fastest time-to-first-token, pay-as-you-go credits, no infra management. Dedicated = reserved GPU pools, lower per-token variability, predictable throughput, ideal when you need predictable SLOs. Private/VPC = customer-managed network, full control over keys and audit, used for regulated PII. note: moving to private typically requires a few weeks setup and ent infra collaboration.
[03:55] Mia Torres: latency numbers? our SLAs need p99 under 300ms for short prompts (<256 tokens).
[04:02] Priya Suresh: on hosting our smaller models can hit p95 ~120-200ms for shorts; p99 250-350ms depending on load. Dedicated usually gives tighter tails since you avoid noisy neighbors. private depends on your connectivity and on-prem hardware.
[04:22] Jacob Rivera: okay that aligns. cost tradeoffs?
[04:25] Priya Suresh: hosted is generally higher per-token but lower ops overhead. Dedicated reduces unit cost at committed spend. Private has highest setup/ops cost but gives control & potentially lower unit cost if you amortize hardware.

[04:45] Sarah Li: do you do model quantization or specific kernels to reduce cost?
[04:49] Priya Suresh: yes we have quantized model variants and kernel selection in the runtime. Redwood Optimize can recommend quant and batch configs for your workload. we can run bench to show token/sec and cost delta.

---

[05:15] Jacob Rivera: for the pilot we want to: 1) run hosted quickstart with a dev team using free credits 2) run a 1-week benchmark against our sample data measuring latency/cost/quality 3) evaluate dedicated vs hosted based on results. does that flow make sense?
[05:29] Alex Chen: totally. typical playbook: issue credits, provide quickstart repo, schedule an SE assist call during bench, deliver a comparison sheet with perf and cost.
[05:39] Noah Patel: we can also set up telemetry hooks to your console so you can see token breakdowns.

[05:48] Mia Torres: are there issues with CORS or embedding dev clients? we'll be building a browser-based dev tool.
[05:54] Priya Suresh: for browser we recommend proxying through your backend or using short-lived keys. direct browser keys are possible but require strong rotation. we have examples in the quickstart.

--- Security deep dive (abbreviated) ---

[06:20] Ethan Park: SOC2 report? where can we see it?
[06:23] Priya Suresh: we'll send the SOC2 Type II summary in the security pack. also have ISO mention in the docs - i'll include the link.
[06:31] Ethan Park: KMS — do you integrate with our AWS KMS or do you force your own?
[06:34] Priya Suresh: for Private/VPC you can use your KMS/HSM; for Hosted we have BYO-KMS options for enterprise where we bring a dedicated envelope key that you control. we need to coordinate the key exchange pattern.
[06:46] Ethan Park: SSO and SCIM?
[06:48] Alex Chen: SSO via SAML or OIDC, SCIM for provisioning, RBAC granular roles. Priya will share the SSO runbook.
[06:56] Jacob Rivera: encryption in transit and at rest?
[06:58] Priya Suresh: TLS 1.2+ in transit, AES-256 at rest. for private you can mount KMS.

---

[07:20] Sarah Li: curious about fallback behavior — if a model scale is constrained can you failover to a cheaper variant?
[07:26] Priya Suresh: yes smart routing can fallback to compatible variants; Redwood supports automatic fallback policies to lower-cost or higher-latency models, also region fallback.

[07:40] Mia Torres: what about on-prem? we have legacy infra that could host inference, any reference for that?
[07:46] Priya Suresh: we have an on-prem package for air-gapped, but timelines are longer. for most customers we start hosted, then if needed we'll pilot VPC + private control plane.

--- Transcript noise and small talk ---
[08:10] Speaker 6: (muffled) sorry incoming fire alarm at my end.
[08:15] Alex Chen: no worries, go ahead.

--- Pilot logistics ---
[08:40] Jacob Rivera: how do we measure quality regressions? we want to tie to our golden prompts and hold stats.
[08:47] Priya Suresh: Redwood Optimize supports eval sets and regression alerts — you upload prompt/expected outputs and we run periodic evals; alerts fire on drift. we can include that in the bench.
[08:58] Sarah Li: can we get per-token cost projection based on our workload?
[09:03] Noah Patel: yes if you share sample QPS and prompt lengths, we can model cost for hosted vs dedicated.

--- Closing and recap ---
[09:15] Alex Chen: recap — we'll: 1) send 50k credits and quickstart link 2) share security pack + SOC2 snapshot 3) schedule a bench assist SE session (Priya) next week 4) Jacob confirms dataset and latency targets.
[09:33] Jacob Rivera: sounds good. target bench week 10/27.
[09:38] Ethan Park: please include KMS integration note in the pack.
[09:41] Mia Torres: i'll loop in two engineers after call.
[09:44] Alex Chen: great thanks everyone — we'll follow up with the assets.

[09:50] (meeting ends)

Notes about transcription: occasional mis-heard words (e.g., "ttft" transcribed as "t-t-f-t"), some speaker labels generic. references: quickstart repo https://redwood.example/quickstart, security pack link placeholder https://redwood.example/security-pack, perf sheet will be shared as Google Sheet link on follow-up.
